newsitem.title: USA: Boeing to build $9 billion network for Teledesic.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to build $9 billion network for Teledesic.

text.p: Boeing Co. will build a $9 billion network of communications satellites as part of a partnership with Teledesic Inc., a communications company owned partly by Microsoft Corp. Chairman Bill Gates, the companies said Tuesday.

Boeing will also invest up to $100 million in Teledesic, giving it a 10 percent stake in the privately held company, whose other primary investor is Craig McCaw, who built the world's largest cellular telephone company.

As the prime contractor, Boeing will lead an international effort to design, build and launch the Teledesic network, which will comprise several hundred low-orbit satellites that will provide telecommunications services such as broadband Internet access, videoconferencing and interactive multimedia.

The agreement brings together McCaw, Teledesic's chairman, who built the world's largest cellular phone company before selling it to AT&T in 1994; Gates, who has built the world's largest computer software company; and Phil Condit, chairman and chief executive officer of the world's largest commercial aicraft maker.

"Our relationship with Teledesic is the perfect catalyst for bringing together all of our historical investments in the space business with our recent and planned investments in Sea Launch, Rockwell and McDonnell Douglas," said Condit.

Using the planned Teledesic network, enterprises will be able to connect branch offices throughout the world to their existing global networks, and workers will be able to telecommute from anywhere, the companies said.
Boeing's stock, which was hurt by a disappoiting earnings report Monday, added $1.50 to $96.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues.
